## The legal basis

These alerts are possible because of a federal disclosure law. The Stock Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act requires U.S. Senators and Representatives to publicly file and disclose any financial transaction within 45 days of its occurrence. Platforms monitor these public filings and push them to subscribers. Trades are sourced from official congressional disclosures: the U.S. House Clerk's Financial Disclosure portal and the Senate Office of Public Records' Electronic Filing system.

One important nuance: "real-time" refers to the **filing**, not the trade itself. Because members have up to 45 days to report, alerts notify you the moment a disclosure is published, but the underlying trade may be weeks old.

Its Pro plan ($5/mo or $48/yr) provides a real-time feed with no delay, personal alerts via email, Telegram, Discord, and push, plus watchlist rules with min-amount and buy/sell filters. **Capitol Gains** is a native iOS app with AI-driven detection. You can bookmark members to track and get push notifications when they trade, when notable transactions are detected, or when large trades hit. Its AI parses raw PDF filings, resolves tickers, maps committee assignments, and scores each trade for significance in real time.

**PoliTrackr** is a focused, email-based alerting tool. It's purely a monitoring and alert app that tracks stock trades disclosed by U.S. Congress members, automatically monitoring new filings and sending an email summary when tracked members disclose a stock purchase or sale. Manually tracking these trades is genuinely painful because checking congressional stock trades means looking at two completely different government systems — the House Clerk Financial Disclosure portal and the Senate EFD search system — each with its own interface, data format, and quirks. Good third-party tools consolidate both feeds into one place and notify you automatically.

One thing worth setting expectations on: no tool can give you truly "real-time" trades, because the STOCK Act gives members up to 45 days from the date of the trade to file their disclosure, and in practice, many members file closer to the deadline, and some file late.
